newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia guided by ACCC on Westpac deal.
newsitem.headline: Australia guided by ACCC on Westpac deal.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday the government would be guided by its competition watchdog ACCC on the planned merger of Westpac Banking Corporation and the Bank of Melbourne Ltd.
"That offer will have to clear the ACCC (Australian Competition and Consumer Commission)," Costello told reporters after releasing Australia's financial system inquiry report.
"It will have to clear the prudential regulator," Costello said.
"But the policy I announce, which is we will not allow mergers between the big four (banks) of course do not apply in relation to regional banks."

Costello, announcing the government's response to the financial inquiry, said the so-called six pillar policy banning mergers or takeovers among Australia's four major banks and two largest life offices would be abolished.
But he said mergers between the four banks would not be allowed at this stage.
Westpac announced earlier this month an A$1.435 billion friendly bid for the Bank of Melbourne, based in the Victorian state capital.
